items.title: Ed Shaughnessy Part II interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 25, 1998 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: Once I started out with a couple of these traveling bands, like Randy Brooks and Bobby Byrne who were second or third layer bands... good bands and good leaders

ctx.x: Oh let’s say it was a struggle to find enough work.

Well I’m a very lucky guy because the only time that I had that was in the beginning. I worked at the phone company, I’d had a couple of day jobs, and I only worked a few gigs at night, and I can honestly tell you that from the age of less than 18, about 17-1/2, I was earning a living at music. It was a small living, but I didn’t have to work a day job anymore. See I graduated high school at 16, so I worked at the phone company from 16 ‘till about 17-1/2, and I put in my union card. You had to establish residence…
Do you think your father was pleased that that little drum set he brought home that day turned into a career for you?
